title: NY State Senate · District 16
area: Northeast Queens, including Flushing, College Point, Whitestone, Bayside and Auburndale.

context.text: Incumbent John Liu is unopposed on the general-election ballot. Philip Wang had filed to run on the Republican and "4 Our Immigrants Party" lines but withdrew or was disqualified before the primary.

candidates.name: John Liu
candidates.currentRole: NY State Senator, District 16 (since 2023; previously District 11, 2019–2023)

summary.text: John Liu is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for NY State Senate District 16 in northeast Queens. A former New York City Councilmember and New York City Comptroller, he has served in the State Senate since 2019 and chairs the New York City Education Committee. He is running unopposed in the general election.

background.text: Immigrated from Taiwan at age five; lives in Flushing.
Attended Hunter College High School and Bronx High School of Science, then earned a degree in mathematical physics from Binghamton University.
Worked 14 years in the private sector as an actuary, including a managerial role at PricewaterhouseCoopers.
Served on the New York City Council representing Flushing and northeast Queens from 2002 to 2009, then served as New York City Comptroller from 2010 to 2013; ran for mayor of New York City in 2013.
Elected to the State Senate representing District 11 in 2018, taking office in 2019; redistricted to District 16, succeeding Toby Ann Stavisky, in 2023.

priorities.text: Says his approach to policy is about people, not just numbers.
priorities.quote: it's not just about numbers, it's about people

priorities.text: Lists affordable housing, pension security and education funding among his priorities, alongside past work on wage protection and expanding opportunities for minority contractors.

positions.summary: Voted yes on the GREAT Act (S9500-A), creating a statewide virtual power plant program aimed at reducing reliance on fossil-fuel peaker plants, and yes on S7898-A, which requires certain construction contracts to site renewable-energy and energy-storage systems.

record.text: Chairs the Senate's New York City Education Committee; also serves on the Education, Finance, Higher Education, Judiciary, Rules and Transportation committees and the Select Majority Task Force on Diversity in the Judiciary.

Sponsored S10007-A, requiring school districts to give parents of nonpublic-school students with disabilities annual written notice of special-education service request procedures and allowing an expedited review process for New York City parents who missed 2024–25 filing deadlines; passed the Senate 61–0 on June 2, 2026.
Sponsored S10365, extending certain deadlines for the green-roof property tax abatement in cities of one million or more people; signed into law as Chapter 153 on June 26, 2026.
Sponsored S10191, which would raise the New York City marriage ceremony fee to $55 and the marriage license fee to $60; remained in the Senate Judiciary Committee as of May 5, 2026.
Voted yes on S9500-A (GREAT Act), establishing the New York State grid reliability and energy affordability transition program, which passed the Senate 39–21.

Voted yes on S7898-A, requiring certain construction project contracts to include siting of renewable energy systems, energy storage systems or electric major utility transmission facilities, which passed the Senate 39–21.
